METHOD: self_evolverec
COMPARISON MODEL FAMILY: bert4rec. Start from the supplied corrected baseline; keep its backbone family throughout search, including initial proposals, merging and debugging. Do not fall back to SASRec or another model family. Keep seed 42, maximum epochs 200, batches per epoch 200 and the supplied splits/evaluator fixed. All models use LEFT-padded histories: the readout must use the final nonpadding position, never count-1. BERT4Rec uses a reserved mask token with masked-target training and appended-mask inference; do not expose a shifted prediction target through bidirectional input. Preserve checkpoint and embedded predictor consistency. Diagnosis uses family-specific sample_batch and ModelView; keep log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items) compatible. One trained model/checkpoint per category; no independent score fusion.

MANDATORY SINGLE-MODEL EXPERIMENT: train one independent model per category.
Do not implement ensembles, bagging, boosting of independent predictors, stacking,
multi-seed/checkpoint averaging, score/rank voting, mixtures of independently fitted
experts, or neural scores combined with separately fitted transition/popularity scores.
Each category must load exactly one independently trained model/checkpoint at prediction.
Jointly trained internal layers/features of one network are allowed. Four category
models are necessary for routing and do not constitute an ensemble. All hypotheses,
code generation, debugging, reviews and memory use must respect this constraint even
if an upstream generic prompt suggests an ensemble. The host audits the actual
predictor before accepting validation scores; violations fail the trial and consume
their training budget. Do not read other trials or reuse their trained checkpoints.

unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probes expect a BERT4Rec encoder with catalog item embeddings, padding ID 0, and reserved mask ID `itemnum + 1`. Inference retains the latest `L−1` history items, appends a mask, and left-pads to length L. The user representation is `encode_sequence(tokens)[:, -1]`; candidate scores are dot products with item embeddings. The backbone implementation is not supplied here.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, plus `item_emb`, `log2feats`, `predict_score`, and training histories. The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors of matching B×L shape. A temporary embedding pre-hook captures live inference tokens. Diagnosis runs in evaluation/inference mode and restores module modes and Python, NumPy, CPU, and CUDA RNG states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Integrity:** Checks reserved-mask IDs, appended-mask input construction, finite scores, live/reference score agreement, padding invariance, and incorrect-readout controls. Explicit failures gate history sensitivity; unavailable checks remain unknown.
- **Embedding collapse:** Computes rescaled mean pairwise cosine over up to 2,048 catalog embeddings. Higher values indicate greater angular alignment; this alone establishes neither quality nor diversity.
- **Masked-target margins:** Across up to ten batches, measures positive-minus-negative logits only at valid supervised mask positions. Reports mean, tenth percentile, negative-outranking rate, and margin-below-0.5 rate. Larger margins and lower failure rates indicate stronger training-target separation.
- **History sensitivity:** For up to 200 users, recovers each final training event from its preceding history. Reports target score, rank, HR@10, hardest-negative margin, intervention deltas, and top-10 overlap, with user-bootstrap intervals and repeat/explore, length, and popularity strata.

# Perturbation & Tests

Structural fixtures cover empty, short, full-length, and repeated histories. Tests perturb padding embeddings and right-context tokens, omit the appended mask, and use the erroneous `count−1` readout. History interventions remove or mask oldest/newest blocks. Three separate candidate draws remain fixed across interventions. Sensitivity has no universally desirable direction.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, including integrity, collapse, margins, counts, reasons, and sensitivity summaries. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` requests an evidence-grounded JSON interpretation.

Training recovery is not held-out generalization or causal preference evidence. Actual sampler provenance, fresh-process checkpoint/predictor parity, and attention deletion remain uncertified. Category metadata and review attributes are unavailable; no four-category macro is computed.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probes expect a BERT4Rec encoder with catalog item embeddings, padding ID 0, and reserved mask ID `itemnum + 1`. Inference retains the latest `L−1` history items, appends a mask, and left-pads to length L. The user representation is `encode_sequence(tokens)[:, -1]`; candidate scores are dot products with item embeddings. The backbone implementation is not supplied here.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, plus `item_emb`, `log2feats`, `predict_score`, and training histories. The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors of matching B×L shape. A temporary embedding pre-hook captures live inference tokens. Diagnosis runs in evaluation/inference mode and restores module modes and Python, NumPy, CPU, and CUDA RNG states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Integrity:** Checks reserved-mask IDs, appended-mask input construction, finite scores, live/reference score agreement, padding invariance, and incorrect-readout controls. Explicit failures gate history sensitivity; unavailable checks remain unknown.
- **Embedding collapse:** Computes rescaled mean pairwise cosine over up to 2,048 catalog embeddings. Higher values indicate greater angular alignment; this alone establishes neither quality nor diversity.
- **Masked-target margins:** Across up to ten batches, measures positive-minus-negative logits only at valid supervised mask positions. Reports mean, tenth percentile, negative-outranking rate, and margin-below-0.5 rate. Larger margins and lower failure rates indicate stronger training-target separation.
- **History sensitivity:** For up to 200 users, recovers each final training event from its preceding history. Reports target score, rank, HR@10, hardest-negative margin, intervention deltas, and top-10 overlap, with user-bootstrap intervals and repeat/explore, length, and popularity strata.

# Perturbation & Tests

Structural fixtures cover empty, short, full-length, and repeated histories. Tests perturb padding embeddings and right-context tokens, omit the appended mask, and use the erroneous `count−1` readout. History interventions remove or mask oldest/newest blocks. Three separate candidate draws remain fixed across interventions. Sensitivity has no universally desirable direction.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, including integrity, collapse, margins, counts, reasons, and sensitivity summaries. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` requests an evidence-grounded JSON interpretation.

Training recovery is not held-out generalization or causal preference evidence. Actual sampler provenance, fresh-process checkpoint/predictor parity, and attention deletion remain uncertified. Category metadata and review attributes are unavailable; no four-category macro is computed.
